extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students in functional analysis/operator theory
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of textbook exercises in functional analysis (Hilbert/Banach spaces, operators, projections, monotone operators, spectral theory, compact and Hilbert–Schmidt operators, Krein–Rutman). Each problem asks to check properties, prove existence/uniqueness, convergence, spectral descriptions, and deduce consequences using standard tools (projections, Opial’s lemma, Stampacchia/Minty–Browder, Fredholm theory, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 27 — Alternate projections (contraction/sequence estimates and convergence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check projection inequalities |P_K u − P_K v|^2 ≤ (P_K u − P_K v, u − v) ≤ |u − v|^2; define alternating projections sequence u_{n+1}=P_{1/2}u_n for two closed convex sets K1,K2 and prove: comparisons between iterates for different starts, monotonicity of distances |u_n − v_n|, convergence of differences |u_{2n} − u_{2n−1}| to d = dist(K1,K2), existence of z = P_K 0 with |z|=d and (z,w) ≥ |z|^2 for w∈K2−K1, and that u_{2n}−u_{2n−1} → z; under an extra hypothesis prove weak convergence of subsequences to points a1∈K1,a2∈K2 with a2−a1=z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes steps: prove pairwise inequalities between iterates; deduce nonincreasing sequences; choose approximating points in K2 to bound limits; set z = P_{K2−K1}0 and estimate |z − (u_{2n}−u_{2n−1})|^2; use Opial’s lemma (see Exercise 5.25) and a construction in H×H with K = { [b1,b2] : b2−b1=z } to get weak limits. Hints: geometric interpretation; show K convex/closed; show boundedness if one set bounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 28 — Projections and orthogonal projections (algebraic and geometric characterizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify basic properties of projections P (P^2=P): I−P projection, nullspaces and ranges relations, decomposition H = N(P)+N(I−P); characterize orthogonal projections by equivalent conditions (P self-adjoint, P^* = P, P^*P ≤ I, N(P) ⟂ N(I−P)); for T with T^*=T and T^2=I, show (I−T)/2 is an orthogonal projection and converse; for closed subspaces M,N with orthogonal projections P=PM, Q=PN prove equivalences of PQ=QP, PQ projection, identify PQ as orthogonal projection onto M∩N and P+Q−PQ onto M+N; give equivalent properties when M ⟂ N, and when M ⊂ N (various algebraic/inequality characterizations and descriptions of Q−P as orthogonal projection onto M^⊥∩N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check equivalences by algebraic manipulation of projections, use properties of ranges and nullspaces, and verify orthogonality conditions. Several small equivalence proofs and geometric remarks (closedness of sum when orthogonal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 29 — Iterates of nonlinear contractions; ergodic theorems (Opial/Baillon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T:H→H be a nonexpansive mapping with nonempty fixed point set K. Define ergodic averages σ_n = (1/n)∑_{i=0}^{n−1} T^i f and μ_n = (1/n)∑_{i=0}^{n−1} (I+T)/2 T^i f. Prove: (A) σ_n and μ_n converge weakly to fixed points of T; (B) if T is odd then both sequences converge strongly. For linear T see related exercises. Provide auxiliary estimates: monotonicity of |T^n f − v|, bounds |σ_n − Tσ_n| ≤ (1/√n)|f − Tσ_n|, property (P) from Exercise 5.25, and convergence arguments using Opial/Baillon techniques and averaging tricks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: show boundedness, use telescoping/inequality sums; derive square-sum bounds ∑|μ_n−μ_{n+1}|^2 ≤ |f−v|^2 and rate |μ_n−Sμ_n| ≤ (1/√{n+1})|f−v|; for odd T use additional inner-product limit arguments and uniform convergence in lag to upgrade weak to strong convergence; use averaging and estimates (detailed steps A1–A5 and B1–B6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 30 — Variants of Stampacchia and von Neumann min–max (existence for variational inequalities and saddle points)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: For continuous bilinear nonnegative form a(·,·) and closed convex K, given f and a v0 with a boundedness condition, prove existence of u∈K solving a(u,v−u) ≥ (f,v−u) ∀v∈K (recover Stampacchia). B: For coercive bilinear b and convex l.s.c. ϕ with nonempty domain, prove unique u∈D(ϕ) satisfying b(u,v−u)+ϕ(v)−ϕ(u)≥0 ∀v. C: For finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces H1,H2 and continuous bilinear F(λ,μ), show existence of saddle point (λ,μ) achieving min_max = max_min, deduce equality of min max and max min and converse. D: Extend to reflexive Banach spaces with K(u,v) convex l.s.c. in u and concave u.s.c. in v and prove min_max = max_min by contradiction using finite convex combinations and C1 arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: perturbations f_ε and a_ε, pass to limit as ε→0 (A); use epi ϕ embedding in H×R and apply A1 (B); use compactness/finite-dimensional reductions for C; construct Bu, Av sets and use finite subcover/combination arguments and earlier C1 result to reach contradiction in D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 31 — Monotone operators; Minty–Browder theorem (existence for inequalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: For monotone A:D(A)⊂E→E* and nonempty bounded closed convex K, prove existence u∈K with ⟨A v, u−v⟩ ≥ 0 ∀v∈D(A)∩K by considering sets K_v = {u∈K: ⟨A v, v−u⟩ ≥0} and applying a finite-dimensional min-max argument. B: If D(A)=E, A monotone and continuous, show existence of u∈K with ⟨A u, w−u⟩ ≥0 for every bounded closed convex K; extend to unbounded K under a boundedness assumption on {u∈K: ⟨A u,u⟩ ≤0}; deduce surjectivity of A under coercivity at infinity; in Hilbert case prove I+A is bijective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key steps: prove K_v closed/convex, extract finite subcollection with empty intersection, form bilinear F and apply a saddle-point result from Problem 30 to produce u as convex combination; use perturbation and truncation arguments for unbounded K; use coercivity limit to show surjectivity; for Hilbert space, use Riesz identification to show I+A bijective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 32 — Kirszbraun–Valentine extension (Schoenberg method)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: For finite index set I and ϕ(u)=max_{i∈I}(|u−y_i|^2−c_i), show unique minimizer u0 exists, derive first-order inclusion u0 ∈ conv{y_i : i∊J(u0)} and converse; extend to maxima of convex C1 fi. B: Given two families (x_i),(y_i) with pairwise contractions |y_i−y_j| ≤ |x_i−x_j|, prove for any p∈H there exists q∈conv{y_i} with |q−y_i| ≤ |p−x_i| ∀i by minimizing ϕ(u)=max_i{|u−y_i|^2−|p−x_i|^2} and applying A3. C: Extend to infinite index sets and conclude that any contraction S defined on D⊂H extends to a contraction T on all H with T(H) ⊂ conv S(D) (use Zorn’s lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: use convexity and first-order optimality (max of convex functions), represent subgradient via convex hull; for extension use finite approximations and compactness arguments; for infinite index/extension use Zorn's lemma and question C1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 33 — Multiplication operator in L^p (domain, closedness, spectrum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A: D(A)→E be multiplication by measurable a(x) on L^p. Prove density of D(A), closedness, characterize when D(A)=E ⇔ a∈L^∞, identify N(A) and its orthogonal complement, determine adjoint A*, domain and nullspace, give surjectivity criterion (|a|≥α a.e.). Assuming a∈L^∞: determine eigenvalues and spectrum σ(A) ⊂ [ess inf a, ess sup a], show endpoints belong to spectrum; for open sets in R^N and continuous bounded a, show σ(A)=a(Ω); show σ(A)={0} iff a=0 a.e.; if measure has no atoms, show A compact ⇔ a=0 a.e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: approximate by truncation un(x)=(1+n^{-1}|a(x)|)^{-1}u(x) for density; use closed graph theorem for equivalence with bounded multiplier; use essential range analysis for spectrum and eigenvalue criteria; use atomless measure arguments for compactness (no nontrivial compact multiplier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 34 — Spectral analysis of the Hardy operator (various spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze T u(x)= (1/x)∫_0^x u(t)dt as an operator on different Banach spaces: A: on E=C([0,1]) prove T∈L(E), compute point spectrum EV(T)=(0,1], determine eigenfunctions, operator norm=1, spectral radius and resolvent formula, surjectivity properties, and compactness into L^q; B: on E=C^1([0,1]) with C^1-norm, show EV(T)=(0,1/2]∪{1} and σ(T)=[0,1/2]∪{1}; C: on E=L^p(0,1) (1<p<∞) show boundedness with norm ≤ p/(p−1), point spectrum EV(T)=(0,p/(p−1)), operator norm = p/(p−1), σ(T)=[0,p/(p−1)], determine adjoint T* and compactness into L^q for q<p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: check continuity and sup-norm bounds; for spectral computations compute explicit resolvent (T−λI)^{-1} when possible; use integrability and Hardy-type inequalities and integration-by-parts trick for L^p estimate; use approximation operators T_ε and compact embedding arguments for compactness claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 35 — Cotlar’s lemma (operator sum norm bound via off-diagonal decay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: For T∈L(H) show ‖T^*T‖=‖T‖^2 and related norm equalities for powers and self-adjoint case. B: For finite family (T_j)_{j=1}^m in L(H) satisfying off-diagonal operator-norm decay bounds ‖T_j T_k^*‖^{1/2} ≤ ω(j−k) and symmetrically, define σ = ∑_{i=−(m−1)}^{m−1} ω(i) and U = ∑_{j=1}^m T_j. Prove ‖U‖ ≤ σ by bounding high powers (U^*U)^N using combinatorial expansion and the ω-decay hypothesis and then taking roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key steps: expand products, estimate each term by chain of ω factors, count combinatorial multiplicity ≤ m, deduce ‖(U^*U)^N‖ ≤ m σ^{2N} and take Nth root letting N→∞ to get ‖U‖ ≤ σ. Use identities from part A for norms of products/powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 36 — Riesz–Fredholm theory (chains of ranges and kernels; finite ascent/descent)
rubrics_metrics.description: For T∈K(E) define N_k=N((I−T)^k), R_k=R((I−T)^k). Prove inclusions R_{k+1}⊂R_k, closedness, eventual stationarity R_k=R_{k+1} for k≥p, finite-dimensionality of N_k and eventual stationarity of N_k; show codim R_k = dim N_k, existence of decomposition E = R_p ⊕ N_p with Rp∩Np={0}, and (I−T) bijective on R_p. For self-adjoint compact T on Hilbert space show p=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compactness to show finite-dimensionality and index-stabilization; apply rank-nullity and finite-rank perturbation arguments; in self-adjoint case use spectral theory to force p=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 37 — Courant–Fischer min–max principle and Rayleigh–Ritz
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-adjoint compact nonnegative T on separable H with eigenvalues μ_k in nonincreasing order and eigenbasis (e_j): prove variational characterizations μ_k = min_{x∈E_k, x≠0} R(x) = max_{x∈E_{k−1}^⊥, x≠0} R(x), show the general min–max max_{dim S=k} min_{x∈S ackslash{0}} R(x)=μ_k, and dual characterizations involving codimension-k−1 subspaces; show monotonicity comparing eigenvalues of compressions S= P_V T|_V to μ_k (ν_k ≤ μ_k), and convergence of eigenvalues for increasing subspaces V(n) with dense union to the true μ_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orthogonality of eigenspaces and Rayleigh quotient properties, show relevant intersections nontrivial to get bounds, and apply spectral approximation arguments for Galerkin convergence (Rayleigh–Ritz).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 38 — Fredholm–Noether operators (equivalent characterizations and index properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: Prove equivalence of (1) R(T) closed with finite codimension and N(T) admits a complement, (2) existence S,F compact such that T◦S = I_F + K, and (3) existence U and finite-rank projection P with T◦U = I_F − P; deduce relations between dimensions. B: Dual set of equivalent conditions for finite-dimensional kernel. C: Define Fredholm operators (FN) and index ind T = dim N(T) − codim R(T); prove existence of U and finite-rank projections realizing T◦U=I−P and U◦T=I−P̃, define pseudoinverse, show stability under adjoint, compact perturbations, small norm perturbations, homotopy invariance of index, composition formula ind(T2∘T1)=ind T1 + ind T2, and compute index for finite-dimensional examples and shift operators. D: Work through examples (finite-dimensional, shift operators) to compute indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: construct complements and inverses on ranges, use finite-rank projections and compact operator perturbation results, invoke known propositions on closed range and complements, apply matrix-family homotopy trick for composition index; use concrete bases for examples (shift operators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 39 — Square root of self-adjoint nonnegative operator (existence/uniqueness and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: For S self-adjoint with 0≤S≤I, show ‖S^2‖=‖S‖^2 ≤1 and 0≤S^2≤S≤I; polynomials with nonnegative coefficients preserve positivity. B: For T self-adjoint, T≥0, ‖T‖≤1 construct iterative sequence S_{n+1}=S_n + (1/2)(T−S_n^2) starting with S_0=I, prove monotonicity and convergence in operator norm to S≥0 with S^2=T and ‖S‖≤1. C: Uniqueness: for U≥0 show unique V≥0 with V^2=U; prove commutation properties with operators commuting with U, show norms relation ‖U^{1/2}‖ = ‖U‖^{1/2}; for commuting positive operators product remains positive. D: For compact U≥0 compute square root V in eigenbasis and show V is compact and specify eigenvalues (square roots of eigenvalues of U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: use polynomial functional calculus and monotone approximation by polynomials with nonnegative coefficients; use iterative scheme and show monotone decreasing differences; uniqueness via comparison on range and nullspace; for compact case use spectral decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 40 — Hilbert–Schmidt operators (definitions, norms, kernels, and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A: Define Hilbert–Schmidt operators HS(E,F) by ∑_k |T e_k|^2 < ∞ for any orthonormal basis; show basis-independence, define HS-norm ‖T‖_{HS}=(∑|T e_k|^2)^{1/2}, show ‖T‖ ≤ ‖T‖_{HS}, linearity, completeness (HS is Hilbert), inclusion HS⊂K, finite-rank ⊂ HS, duality T∈HS↔T^*∈HS with equal norms, characterization for compact self-adjoint operators via eigenvalues (∑λ_k^2<∞), composition properties (T2∘T1 ∈ HS if one factor HS), inverse-type results for I+T with T∈HS, and existence of orthonormal basis of HS given rank-one operators. B: For E=F=L^2(Ω) and K∈L^2(Ω×Ω) define (T u)(x)=∫ K(x,y)u(y)dy. Show T bounded with operator and HS norm bounded by L^2 norm of kernel; conversely any HS operator has unique L^2 kernel; compute HS-norm for Hardy-type operator on (0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: use orthonormal expansions and tensor-product bases ej⊗ek for L^2(Ω×Ω); estimate via Parseval; show compactness by truncating expansions; construct kernel by matrix coefficients t_{j,k}=(T e_k, e_j) and sum t_{j,k} e_j⊗e_k in L^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem 41 — Krein–Rutman theorem (positive compact operator, leading eigenvalue/vector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be a closed convex cone in Banach space E with nonempty interior and P≠E. For compact operator T with T(P ackslash{0}) ⊂ Int P, prove existence of x0∈Int P and μ0>0 with T x0 = μ0 x0; moreover establish uniqueness up to scalar of positive eigenvector and spectral gap: any eigenvector in P ackslash{0} corresponds to μ0 and is proportional to x0, and any eigenvalue μ for general x satisfies either μ=μ0 with x scalar multiple of x0 or |μ|<μ0. Provide construction via the nonlinear map F(x)=T((x+u)/‖x+u‖) on P with Schauder fixed point and limiting arguments with ε→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: choose u∈Int P and r>0 with T u − r u ∈ P; study the map F and apply Schauder fixed point; obtain family x_ε solving T(x_ε + εu)=λ_ε x_ε with λ_ε≥r, show boundedness and pass to limit to get x0,μ0; uniqueness/maximum property uses order-interval τ(a,b) and a comparison argument to rule out different eigenvalues/eigenvectors in cone.
